item.title: Denle Chayote
item.description: This work is an attempt to delve into the complexities of identity, culture, and human connection while drawing inspiration from the narrative styles of TV and YouTube shows. Through the humanised character of a chayote, I explore themes of post-colonialism and cultural exchange, primarily inspired by my experiences in Oaxaca, Mexico. With a blend of humour and introspection, the viewer is invited to join me on a personal journey of exchange, fostering a deeper understanding of the shared human experience.

item.title: that's you in the spotlight
item.description:
This work plays with the precarious nature of being seen (or even consumed) by the media we consume. It further layers an aspect of an alt-Hindu guru/diva figure whose virtual presence provides the audience with flimsy guidance and support as they find their image absorbed by the work. While you reminisce the inherent nostalgia of R.E.M’s Losing My Religion, she will help you either find or lose your faith.

love and thanks to:
Inna Kuzminova for the beautiful 3D backgrounds
Martina Svobodová for the lovely introductory vocals

item.title: LyrArkestra+
item.description:
LyrArkestra+ was a collaborative project within which I created visuals along with Cristina and Isa.

The project focused on performing graphic scores primarily by Czech and Slovak composers in unconventional audiovisual renditions. The international ensemble of this essentially fluid project does not have a permanent team. The audio composition were developed and performed by Tomáš Knoflíček (Gurun Gurun) from Ostrava, Michal Zbořil (IQ+1, B4) from Přerov, Daniel Jakeš (Jasnovidec, Koroze) from High Tatras, Ken Ganfield (PIO, The MoND) from Ames, Martin Nábělek (Boyse) from Banská Bystrica, and Petr Vrba (Poisonous Frequencies, Banausoi) from Prague. All sounds originated in the Lyra synthesizer, which is described as “organismic”, i.e. close to living organisms in its internal interactions and functioning on the basis of imaginary “conversations” between the individual modules…The musical component is complemented by the visuals of Cristina Maldonado, Keya Singh and Isa Juchniewicz, who has created a structured digital environment that both responds directly to the music and allows for an additional layer of improvisation.

item.title: Caring to Grow
item.description:
feat. Bajza, Jullie, Alžbeta and Lia

Each of them has a story to tell through their affection and passion for plants. This work is about memory, connections, recognition and reflection. We can always learn something from each other.The seemingly ordinary always has something special in it because of how specific each of us are.

Its suuuper exciting (!!) to see people love so deeply that it nourishes them and people around them.
The Slovak dialogues were translated by amoebadam and all the subtitling was done by Lamija Čehajić + me.

item.title: Zangezi
item.description: “Zangezi is a sextet accompanied by a “visual artist” and a “sound designer” that strives for an artificial but organic sound production aesthetic." As the visual artist in this sextet, I composed the live-visuals in this piece along with camera support from Hoi Man. Much of the visuals were created with live-camera input along with elements made using footage filmed the day before during our rehearsals. In this work, the visuals mainly played with temporality and multiplicity of the image.

item.title: Intimate Immensity
item.description: In 2019, as part of a collective, I explored overlapping presences in a mixed reality performance with the use of immersive video in Insider. I decided to expand the technical challenge towards virtual reality and started imagining an XR installation. This led to my conceptual research on Char Davies, embodiment in VR and the dialogue between virtual-real stimuli. The title Intimate Immensity was taken from The Poetics of Space by Gaston Bachelard. While reading this text, I found myself strongly moved by the poetic images of introspection as affected by different spaces and isolation. My experiences during the pandemic elevated my need to connect with the outside world. However, these times also showed me the importance of self-awareness and reflection. And while VR may often be used as an escape from reality, it can very well ground us in the present.

item.title: learning about validation
item.description: Self-reflection comes through even more clearly often with the help of others. When you work with people who see you as someone who’s more than a colleague, the work becomes easier and arguably better. My work with video so far has allowed me to meet and interact with wonderful people who continue to support me and help me grow as an artist. This work is about them teaching me validation while simultaneously being a portrait of each of them.

Growing up, I watched my father dance to Ishq Tera Tadpave with such joy that it was infectious. I started mimicking his moves, and it soon became our song. It also became the song I could dance to without worrying about how I look or if people were looking at me funny. Inadvertently our dance routine helped my self-esteem/image.

item.title: Rickey Mouse saga
item.description: Rickey Mouse Fun House was a project led by Finnish artist, Pasi Mäkelä. I initially joined this constellation in the role of support camera and video editor during their first performance which was live streamed from Punctum (Prague, CZ) in December 2020. From the following year, I began creating the live-visuals we would use in the show. Spiritually and formally rooted in experiment and play, this project was genuinely fun to be a part of. I was able to come in and develop all the live-camera things I wanted to play with, while also learning how these phenomenal musicians improvised together using specific counting systems and timing to enhance the audience’s listening experience as well as their own experiences of playing live music. I developed my practise of working with the simplicity of OBS Studio and pushing its limits by building visuals using chroma/luma keying, layering, collaging, screen inputs, source repetition, multiple camera inputs and multiple projections.

item.title: LAB_D'epog
item.description:
I was asked to create a video using curated archive footage by Matyaš Dlab (dramaturg) and Lucia Repasska (director) of D’epog. This work was made in collaboration with a Ukrainian artist, John Object.

The idea was to play with the infectious, chaotic energy that D’epog exudes. I decided to build the narrative around an understated metaphor of screens as an observation of self while slowing and stretching time.

item.title: Lunchmeat Festival 2020
item.description:
About
    #

    I made live visuals for Evil Medvěd’s modular set at Lunchmeat Festival 2020. The visuals came from my visual language around self, identity and social action - reacting to what Evil Medvěd was doing live. With live manipulation of the visuals using a MIDI keyboard, I was able to react in realtime, creating a sequence of images that occurred only once within the confines of this set.

item.title: Plechy a neplechy
item.description: While interning at Teren in 2020, I filmed and edited a series of videos for a sound performance produced at Centrum Experimentálního Divadla (CED) Brno. This event featured performances by Petr Válek, Ondřej Merta, and Marie Komarová, and was organized in cooperation with Vašulka Kitchen Brno and Bastl Instruments.

item.title: #jpeg2dicom
item.description:
Ongoing experiments using a CT scan reader to compress video frames into objects that can be manipulated in 3D. This curiosity was born while attending an online workshop, “Creative and Artistic Use of Medical Imagery” led by Haraldur Karlsson and organised by Vašulka Kitchen Brno in April-May 2020.

Since the workshop, I have been testing material in terms of footage (filmed, found, images in motion) and colours. My aim for the future is to convert these objects into 3D files that can be used in 3D and VR environments.

item.title: Insider
item.description:
About
    #

    Insider is a mixed reality performative exploration of the senses focusing on notions of embodiment and body ownership. It’s a performance for 1 audience member at a time. Each audience member is accompanied by a performer who facilitates the experience. Choices made by the audience members can create unique experiences for each person who sees this work.

item.title: Insider: unwrapping reality/opening
item.description:
We have adapted Insider into installations for opening events to reach audiences outside the performance schedules. Each installation explores various elements of the work while adapting to the theme of the hosting event.

These installations were created by a collective of artists - Cristina Maldonado, Keya Singh, Eva Rosemarijn, Lea Kukovičič, Isa Juchniewicz, Lamija Čehajić. Our individual participation at each event changes as needed.

Premiere at CED with Terén

28/11/19, Brno, CZ

item.title: PRTY FR 1
item.description: A (hyper)realistic representation of what it would be like to party with myself with an audiovisual performance by me for me. This work was inspired by strong, vibrant female pop musicians I witnessed while growing up who imbibed a need in me to find a self-image.

item.title: أنا ناقص مني جوا Naqes Meni Juwa
item.description: All my life, I have been hearing others (and myself) constantly comment on my appearance. This work is about being stuck in a loop of choreographed movements that are mainly done to observe my own image while contemplating the hollowness of my actions and being.

item.title: About Global Groove
item.description: An audiovisual presentation of research I did while writing an essay about Global Groove (1973) by Nam June Paik. At that moment in time, this was the most extensively researched and planned video project I had worked on. The writing and planning process prepared me for future projects. The audiovisual language of this video was inspired by Nam June Paik’s work – specifically his editing patterns and vibrant use of colours reflecting the contemporary trends in broadcast television and advertisements.

item.title: Learning to Groove (on Global Groove by Nam June Paik)
You Don't Know Me
item.description: An attempt to confront the outer world with all the faces my inner world can put on while exclaiming the words “You Don’t Know Me” over and over again with varying stress on each word. The rhythm of the video was inspired while exploring the works of Gary Hill.
